item.title: Wife of top ex-Biden advisor easily advances to House showdown in November
item.description: Maggie Goodlander faced challenger Paige Beauchemin in the New Hampshire Democratic primary as the district braces for a reshaped political map.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Maggie Goodlander, D-N.H., won her primary to advance to a general election showdown in a Democrat-leaning seat comprising generally the western half of New Hampshire from Massachusetts to the Canadian border.

Goodlander is the wife of former Biden National Security Adviser Jacob Sullivan, and won her first race for the seat in 2024 – succeeding the retiring Rep. Ann Kuster, D-N.H.

While Republicans have dominated the governor’s office in New Hampshire in recent years, Democrats have been largely successful at the congressional level.

The district has been in Democratic hands since 2013 and, prior to that, largely held by Rep. Charles Bass, R-N.H., who served two lengthy tenures interrupted by a Democrat in the mid-1990s.

TRUMP SAYS US MAY RECOVER ALL THE EQUIPMENT LEFT BEHIND IN AFGHANISTAN BY BIDEN ADMIN

Goodlander faced New Hampshire State Rep. Paige Beauchemin, D-Hillsborough, and there is also an independent running in the general election. The winner of a four-way Republican primary Tuesday night was Goodlander’s last opponent, Lily Tang Williams.

Goodlander’s husband’s role in the White House was prominent, as Sullivan was front-and-center during the disastrous Afghanistan withdrawal in 2021, had a role in foreign relations during the early part of the Russia-Ukraine War and helped manage the U.S. relationship with China.

ONE OF CONGRESS' MOST POWERFUL DEMOCRATS JUST SURVIVED A PROGRESSIVE PRIMARY REVOLT

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Beauchemin ran against Goodlander from the left, arguing the incumbent has not been sufficiently progressive or effective during her first term.

The district is the more rural of the two, and includes cities like Pittsburg in the forests of northern New Hampshire.

With neighboring Rep. Chris Pappas, D-N.H., giving up his House seat to run for the Senate seat being vacated by Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, D-N.H., the political landscape in the Granite State will look much different no matter what come January.

item.title: Ex-NFL star believes Mike McDaniel's 'best decision of his career' was joining Chargers with Justin Herbert
item.description: Shawne Merriman said Mike McDaniel's explosive scheme could unlock a new gear for Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers' playoff hopes.
item.content:encoded:
While one team in Los Angeles is getting all the recognition throughout the NFL, another is gearing up for what they believe will be a season to watch on their front at SoFi Stadium.

The Los Angeles Chargers sharing a home with the Los Angeles Rams might be hard if you're battling for headlines, but this team has the chance to be just as explosive in 2026.

Why? Mike McDaniel joined Jim Harbaugh's staff in L.A. as the team's new offensive coordinator, and he hasn't shied away from his feelings about his quarterback, Justin Herbert, in the slightest throughout training camp. Simply put, he's obsessed with what Herbert can do, to the point where he's expected to be opening up previously locked plays in his explosive scheme.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Former Chargers star linebacker Shawne Merriman has faith his old squad will be back in the playoffs this season, and McDaniel will be a major reason why they could be contending far beyond just representing the AFC come Wild Card weekend.

"I think Mike McDaniel has made the best decision of his career," Merriman told OutKick in a recent interview. "That’s even outside of leaving the San Francisco 49ers. I think they had something fun, an explosive offense at one time with [Jaylen] Waddle, Tyreek Hill and things like that out in Miami. But he had an opportunity to get a head coaching job at a couple of places, and he didn’t feel it was right.

"So, what happens is you take the best position that puts you back in the driver’s seat after this next year or two so you can go take the job you want."

When McDaniel joined the Chargers, he said he was "geeked" to work with Herbert, whom he believes "hasn't neared the ceiling to what he's capable of." That's saying something considering Herbert has thrown for 5,000 yards in his career, and has proven to be among the top talents in the NFL at quarterback.

CHARGERS QUARTERBACK JUSTIN HERBERT AND POP STAR MADISON BEER ANNOUNCE ENGAGEMENT WITH ROMANTIC POST

But McDaniel's words are something that has Chargers fans geeked, too, especially if there's an extra gear he could unlock with the former first-round pick.

"Justin Herbert had to be the biggest influence of going there, because now you have an explosive quarterback," Merriman added. "He’s an explosive offensive coordinator, so the deep balls down the field, we’ve already seen Quentin Johnston down the field – he’s explosive. You’ve got Ladd McConkey who can work the middle of the field and get open in shorter routes. You have a hell of a running back that comes back healthy this year. …They have an explosive opportunity to win."

Merriman even said that McDaniel joining Harbaugh was interesting at first considering their "quirky" nature in terms of how they coach. But it's been a seamless transition thus far, though Week 1 against the Arizona Cardinals will be the true indicator on just how in sync Harbaugh, McDaniel, Herbert and the rest of the team are.

However, no matter how great the Chargers are in the regular season, a dark cloud hangs over the head of the team, especially Herbert, as he has yet to win a playoff game since entering the NFL.

Merriman was very impressed L.A. was even able to reach the playoffs as the No. 7 seed in the AFC last season considering key injuries to players like tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt, linebacker Khalil Mack, rookie running back Omarion Hampton and more. But Herbert seemed to will the team there, while the defense stepped up big time in key moments down the stretch.

The New England Patriots, though, won 16-3 on Wild Card weekend and Herbert suffered his third career playoff loss. It's something that has to change for the Chargers, but Merriman has an optimistic mindset it will this season.

"Justin Herbert’s going to have that dark cloud over him until he gets deep into the playoffs, right? If he wasn’t so talented, I don’t think the expectations would still be so high. But he has all the tools to do it," he said.

"He’s tough as nails. He had that hand [injury], and he battled through it. I just have so much respect for Justin Herbert."

It will be a daunting road for the Chargers to reach the playoffs in general this season despite having an easier start with the Cardinals and Las Vegas Raiders meeting them at home. The Chargers have arguably the toughest schedule in the league facing stretches that include AFC West foes like the Denver Broncos and Kansas City Chiefs twice, while having to travel to the Buffalo Bills, Seattle Seahawks and Baltimore Ravens. They’ll also have to face those Rams in a SoFi Stadium battle on Nov. 1.

But if there was ever a time to prove McDaniel’s offensive scheme is what was needed to change things for the Chargers, this is the ultimate test for a team and fan base begging to make a run at the Vince Lombardi Trophy.

item.title: Cold case takes grim turn after remains identified as runaway teen; homicide investigation underway
item.description: Advanced DNA testing and genetic genealogy identified remains found near a North Carolina manufacturing facility as those of a Maryland teen who vanished in 1977.
item.content:encoded:
Authorities announced a major breakthrough in a decades-old cold case, identifying human remains found nearly 49 years ago in North Carolina as belonging to a runaway 15-year-old girl who disappeared from Maryland.

The skeletal remains were discovered more than six months after Cindy Marcell Blizzard went missing in the spring of 1977, according to the North Carolina State Bureau of Investigation (SBI).

Authorities said the manner of death remained undetermined, but the case was being investigated as a homicide. They said the remains were found in a wooded area near a Wilson County manufacturing facility roughly five hours south of Blizzard's home.

The "circumstances surrounding the location and recovery of the remains raised the probability of foul play, and the investigators are treating the case as a homicide," the SBI said.

TEEN FOUND IN SHALLOW CALIFORNIA VINEYARD GRAVE IDENTIFIED NEARLY 50 YEARS LATER AS FAMILY WARNS KILLER

According to officials, skeletal remains and clothing were found Dec. 29, 1977, near a Firestone plant that produces vehicle tires.

A medical examiner determined the remains had likely been there for six months to two years and belonged to a white female between 16 and 23 years old.

In the decades that followed, the case went cold as forensic technology was not advanced enough to identify the remains, authorities said.

"For years, investigators compared dental records against missing persons cases without finding a match," the SBI said.

GIRL KNOWN AS 'CHELSEA JANE DOE' ID'D 26 YEARS AFTER MUTILATED BODY FOUND HUNDREDS OF MILES FROM HOME STATE

The case was reopened in 2010 by a state anthropologist, who submitted the remains for DNA testing and cross-referenced the results with federal databases, officials said.

However, the investigation did not gain momentum until 2024, when the SBI’s Cold Case Investigative Team reviewed the case again using forensic tools that did not exist in 1977.

WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT

When the case qualified for advanced DNA testing, forensic scientists extracted preserved genetic material from a bone sample, according to the authorities.

"A genealogy service used the profile to trace potential relatives, pointing investigators toward a 15-year-old girl who had run away from Monkton, Maryland, in the spring of 1977," the SBI said.

The identification was made with assistance from the FBI’s NCIC Investigation and Operational Assistance Group, the Maryland Department of State Police Homicide Unit and the Raleigh Police Department’s Intel Unit, authorities said.

Investigators continue to search for answers surrounding Blizzard’s death.

item.title: Establishment Dem defeats socialist challenger in crucial battleground Senate primary
item.description: Chris Pappas defeated Karishma Manzur in the New Hampshire Senate primary, but a heated general election awaits against a former U.S. senator.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Chris Pappas on Tuesday won the Democratic Senate nomination in swing state New Hampshire, in a key race that is a must-hold for the Democrats in the midterm elections.

Pappas defeated socialist rival and first-time candidate Karishma Manzur, the Associated Press reports, in the showdown to succeed retiring longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, the first woman in the nation's history elected governor and senator.

Republicans haven't won a Senate election in New Hampshire in 16 years, but they view the open Democrat-held seat as a top flip opportunity in the fight to hold their slim majority in the midterms.

The race between Pappas and Manzur was one of the final fights in a six-month primary season that saw the far-left score a slew of high-profile victories over centrists in what's been framed as a battle for the Democrats' ideological future.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

Manzur, who saw a surge in support in recent weeks, took the fight to Pappas.

"All he wants to do is just get his little cushy job and go to D.C. Go to all these parties and these restaurants and just do whatever the bare minimum is," she charged in a Fox News Digital interview.

The first-time candidate, scientist with a Ph.D. in biochemistry, and nonprofit leader who is a member of a local Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) group, pushed for universal health care, raising the minimum wage to at least $20 per hour, abolishing ICE, and ending all military aid to Israel for what she argues is the Israeli government's "genocide" against the Palestinian people in their war against Hamas in Gaza.

Manzur argued that Pappas, who has been supported over the years by the pro-Israel lobby AIPAC, is a "genocide enabler."

"Chris Pappas has had his turn and has not been able to serve this state honorably. He hasn't done a good job in serving his corporate donors, his AIPAC foreign-aligned lobbies," she claimed.

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Pappas, in an interview with Fox News Digital, said, "Israel's a historic ally of the United States, the only democracy in the region. And you can say that while you have vehement disagreements with the Netanyahu government as I've expressed."

And referring to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Pappas said, "I think Netanyahu's being incredibly reckless right now. He faces voters in a matter of weeks and could lose his election. And I think that would be important to set a new tone for the U.S.-Israel relationship."

Pappas, who was the frontrunner for his party's nomination ever since Shaheen announced early last year that she wouldn't seek re-election, enjoys strong establishment and union backing. And for over a year, as he runs for the Senate, Pappas also takes aim at what he calls a political system "rigged for billionaires."

Regardless, Manzur charged that Pappas took a page from her playbook.

"It's really embarrassing and insulting to the people of New Hampshire. He's been there for eight years. He has not provided any of that sort of populist messages, and now he's realizing, wait, he's dropping in the polls, and now he has to catch up," Manzur charged. "That's another one of those deceptions that... Chris Pappas always engages in."

CHECK OUT THE LATEST FOX NEWS POLLING IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Pappas defended his record, noting "I've been fighting to change Washington to get big money out of our political system since I got elected to Congress in 2018."

And Pappas emphasized he's "appealing to those voters between the 20 and 80-yard line on the political playing field, and there are a lot of them in New Hampshire. This is not a left-wing or a right -wing state. It's a state of voters who are pragmatic."

Pappas will face off in the general election against either former Sen. John E. Sununu or former Sen. Scott Brown.

Asked how he'll unify his party after a primary showdown that turned heated, Pappas said, "I've always been able to bring people together, and that's how you do things in New Hampshire."

Pointing to the high-stakes head, Pappas said, "Democrats are coming together regardless of how these primaries are shaking out because they understand where the real fight is. This is an election here in New Hampshire that's going to determine the balance of power in the United States Senate. And Democrats won't be able to take the majority back in the US Senate if they don't hold this specific seat here in New Hampshire."

item.title: Incumbent GOP governor rolls to primary victory after keeping Trump at a distance
item.description: Kelly Ayotte cruised past Republican primary challengers, setting up a high-stakes New Hampshire governor's race against Democrat Cinde Warmington.
item.content:encoded:
First-term Republican Governor Kelly Ayotte easily handled her primary opponents Tuesday, setting up a high-stakes general election battle against Democratic gubernatorial nominee Cinde Warmington, who ran unopposed for her party's nomination.

Ayotte defeated Republican challengers Shaun Fife and Bob Wayne McClory as she seeks a second two-year term leading the Granite State.

The former senator and state Attorney General entered Tuesday's primary as the incumbent after winning the governor's mansion in 2024, when Ayotte defeated former Manchester Mayor Joyce Craig and kept the office in Republican hands following the retirement of four-term GOP Gov. Chris Sununu.

KEY SWING STATE VOTERS TO SETTLE DUELING SENATE PRIMARY FIGHTS IN CRUCIAL OPEN-SEAT RACE

Ayotte previously served as New Hampshire's attorney general from 2004 to 2009 before winning election to the U.S. Senate in 2010. She served one term before narrowly losing her 2016 reelection campaign to Democrat Maggie Hassan.

In 2024, following Sununu's decision not to seek a fifth two-year term, Ayotte mounted a political comeback with the outgoing governor's endorsement.

In her first term, Ayotte successfully pushed to roll back portions of the state's bail reform law, arguing the existing system was too lenient on criminal suspects awaiting trial, signed legislation requiring public schools to restrict student cellphone use and pushed penalties for motorists who refuse Breathalyzer tests.

TRUMP-BACKED JOHN E. SUNUNU BREAKS WITH PRESIDENT ON KEY ISSUE AHEAD OF HIGH-STAKES NEW-HAMPSHIRE PRIMARY

Meanwhile, her tenure has faced criticism from the left over a state budget that included cuts to state agencies.

Ayotte will take on Warmington, who served on New Hampshire's five-member Executive Council for two terms, during which she was the lone Democrat on the body that works with the governor to approve state measures and helps consider gubernatorial appointments, among its duties. Tuesday marked her second campaign for governor after Warmington lost the 2024 Democratic gubernatorial primary.

Warmington has attacked Ayotte for failing to adequately stand up to President Donald Trump, citing healthcare cuts, tariffs and the war in Iran.

The Concord Monitor reported in June that Ayotte "steered clear of all things Trump" for much of her first term, noting that, when asked whether she would stand with Trump if he visited New Hampshire, Ayotte responded, "I'm standing with the people of New Hampshire."

item.title: Ex-GOP senator clears hurdle in crucial comeback bid as Republicans try to flip key Senate seat
item.description: John E. Sununu defeated Scott Brown for the GOP Senate nomination in New Hampshire, a key race that could determine Republican majority control.
item.content:encoded:
Former Sen. John E. Sununu on Tuesday won the GOP Senate nomination in swing state New Hampshire, in a race that may determine if Republicans keep control of the chamber in the midterm elections.

Sununu defeated former Sen. Scott Brown, the Associated Press reports, in the showdown to succeed retiring longtime Democratic Sen. Jeanne Shaheen, the first woman in the nation's history elected governor and senator.

Republicans haven't won a Senate election in New Hampshire in 16 years, but they view the open Democrat-held seat as a top flip opportunity in the fight to hold their slim majority in the midterms.

Sununu will now face off in the general election against either four-term Rep. Chris Pappas or socialist candidate and scientist Karishma Manzur, who are battling for the Democratic nomination.

THESE 12 MIDTERM RACES WILL DECIDE WHICH PARTY CONTROLS THE SENATE

Sununu, the son of former Gov. John H. Sununu and older brother to former Gov. Chris Sununu, is a former congressman and senator who is aiming to return to the Senate.

President Donald Trump in February endorsed Sununu, a longtime GOP Trump critic, over Brown, one of Trump's first-term ambassadors. Sununu was also backed by Senate Majority Leader John Thune and the National Republican Senatorial Committee.

Brown charged in a Fox News Digital interview that Sununu's "got 70 endorsements on his website, but he doesn't have the president’s. He never talks about it. He's embarrassed by it."

"I've had the MAGA base and a lot of those so-called traditional Republicans for almost over a year," Brown highlighted. "Johnny came lately, and he's here, and now he thinks everyone's going to just vote for him. That's not how it works. You got to go earn it."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

Brown claimed that Sununu is "beholden" to Trump, Thune, the Senate leadership, and outside groups.

"He owes them everything. He doesn't work for the people of New Hampshire," Brown charged.

But Sununu told Fox News Digital, "I'll have one job stand up for the people of New Hampshire every single day... I don't need to make anyone in Washington happy. It's all about our state, our communities, our economy, and our small businesses."

Asked by about Trump's endorsement, Sununu didn't mention the president's name but highlighted his local endorsements, saying "we've received tremendous support in New Hampshire... we've got great momentum at the grassroots level."

Trump last week said he'd be heading out on the campaign trail to help fellow Republicans running in the midterms.

Asked if he'd like Trump to join him on the Granite State campaign trail, Sununu answered, "I don't need anyone from outside New Hampshire to campaign for me. I've said that from the very beginning."

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The former senator also disagreed with the Trump administration's trade war with neighboring Canada, saying "I don't think it's the right thing to pick a trade war with Canada. They're a great trading partner for New Hampshire."

Republicans are facing a rough political climate heading into the midterms, due persistent inflation, high gas prices fueled by what polls indicate is an unpopular war with Iran, and Trump's underwater approval ratings.

But Sununu, who defeated Shaheen in 2002 to win election to the Senate but lost a rematch to her six years later, said he's "focused on the right things, affordability, bringing down the cost of living on housing, health care, and energy, a reform agenda."

item.title: NFL legend Edgerrin James seeks support for son Jizzle amid unspecified substance abuse battle
item.description: Edgerrin James urged fans not to give his son Jizzle James money or valuables, saying the college basketball transfer is battling a substance abuse issue.
item.content:encoded:
This story may contain details that are disturbing.If you or someone you know is having thoughts of suicide, please contact the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline at 988.

Pro Football Hall of Famer Edgerrin James turned to social media in a public plea for his son, former Charlotte basketball player Jizzle James. The former Indianapolis Colts standout running back said his son is facing a substance abuse issue.

James did not share further details about the issue. He did, however, ask anyone who sees his 21-year-old son to offer him a hug while urging them not to give him anything of value.

"Jizzle is dealing with substance abuse and is NOT in the right state of mind right now," James wrote Tuesday in an Instagram Story post. "If you see him, show him LOVE-but DO NOT give him money, valuables, or anything material."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

James emphasized that his son’s needs are being met and urged those around him to offer encouragement and love. "You’re not helping him by feeding the problem. He wants/needs for NOTHING. Give him a hug. Give him encouragement. Give him love. THAT’S IT. Be patient with him. We’re fighting for him, not against him."

James’ stint as a college basketball player at Charlotte was brief. After spending three seasons with Cincinnati, he transferred to the 49ers earlier this offseason to follow Wes Miller, who left the Bearcats to become Charlotte’s head coach.

According to Charlotte’s sports information department, James is no longer with the program. A spokesperson cited personal issues.

James’ exit from Charlotte followed a turbulent final season with Cincinnati. The Bearcats dismissed him from the program last summer but reinstated him midway through the season. He appeared in 23 games, averaging 10.9 points and 2.1 assists per game.

James averaged 10.8 points per game during his Cincinnati career. He later hinted at a possible reunion with Cincinnati in a social media post, but the school appeared to respond by sending him a cease-and-desist letter.

JAYDEN DANIELS TELLS LSU TO KEEP HIS NAME OUT OF ITS MOUTH IN WILD NO. 5 JERSEY FEUD INVOLVING NIL

"As you are no longer a member of the University of Cincinnati men’s basketball program, you are no longer authorized to use, represent, or commercially promote the University of Cincinnati basketball program, including the use of the University’s name, logos, uniforms, jerseys, or other team-related likenesses," the letter obtained by SI.com read.

"Any sale, advertisement, or distribution of University of Cincinnati basketball jerseys or merchandise representing you as a current player is strictly prohibited."

"I have my own merch I made. I don’t need y’all jerseys," James said in a response posted to Instagram.

item.title: Chris Rock exposes LA's dark ‘underbelly’ that people pretend doesn't exist
item.description: Chris Rock's new film "Misty Green" explores L.A.'s dichotomy of $40 million homes and homelessness as he opens up about fame's dark side in Hollywood.
item.content:encoded:
Chris Rock this week said that Hollywood exposes a dark "underbelly" in Los Angeles that people want to pretend doesn’t exist.

"L.A. is a complicated place, man," the comedian said in an interview with Variety that was published on Tuesday. "Fame’s a complicated thing. I’ve seen the switch in my lifetime."

The 61-year-old said that people who came to Hollywood used to want to be "great — a great singer, great actor, great comedian. Now it’s just fame, and the greatness is almost assumed."

HOLLY MADISON SAYS PLAYBOY MANSION FELT LIKE A 'SAFE HARBOR' AFTER SHE ENCOUNTERED HOLLYWOOD'S DARK SIDE

"I mean, you’re always gonna be outed at some point if you don’t have the goods," he continued. "But L.A. is the mecca of that. It can be beautiful. It’s got the best weather in the world. But it also attracts an underbelly that people want to pretend doesn’t exist."

Rock said he has a home in both New York and Los Angeles, adding that loves "parts" of the West Coast city.

The comedian jokes that he "winters" in California.

DENNIS QUAID DITCHED LA FOR NASHVILLE AFTER THE ONCE 'FANTASTIC' CITY WENT 'DOWNHILL'

The "Everybody Hates Chris" star is directing an indie movie right now, "Misty Green," about a has-been actress living in Los Angeles who’s now broke.

Rock said that movie is "a lot of it’s about L.A. L.A. has got very wonky priorities. There’s a real estate office on the same street as The Ivy on Robertson, and in the window, there are houses for $30-$40 million. In the window. But there’s a homeless guy sleeping right outside. The movie is about that crazy dichotomy."

Rock also reflected on getting slapped by Will Smith at the Academy Awards in 2022 while he was presenting.

"I wish nothing would have happened," he said of incident in which Smith, who went on to win best actor right after, told Rock, "Keep my wife's name out your f-----g mouth!" after the comedian made a joke about Jada Pinkett Smith.

"It’s a crazy world," Rock continued to Variety. "We walk by homeless people. There’s all sorts of s--t going on right now. Me having a bad day is not the biggest — it’s not that important."

"I’m not getting nominated," he said. "The only way I’ll go back is if I’m nominated, and I’m not getting nominated. And that’s OK. We’ll deal with that if it happens. Like, let’s manage expectations."

item.title: Nicolas Cage's Malibu beachfront home damaged after driveway collapses into massive sinkhole
item.description: Video shows a massive 30-by-30-foot sinkhole swallowing Nicholas Cage's oceanfront driveway after Hurricane Marie sent 10-foot waves crashing ashore.
item.content:encoded:
Nicolas Cage's beachfront home was damaged after the driveway collapsed following days of rough surf.

The driveway in front of the Oscar-winning actor's oceanfront home collapsed, creating a sinkhole. Fox 11 reported that the Los Angeles County Fire Department said it was caused by coastal erosion spurred by a hurricane that formed in the Pacific Ocean, Hurricane Marie, generating big waves and high tides.

Video taken of the home shows a 30 by 30 foot hole in front of the home with the waves and the beams holding up his home visible underneath.

Pieces of the glass fence that once stood in front of the driveway, as well as concrete can be seen in the hole, as orange cones set up along the edge.

NICOLAS CAGE LEADS ALL-STAR CAST IN 'FORTITUDE,' A WWII FILM ABOUT THE D-DAY DECEPTION CAMPAIGN

The City of Malibu released a statement regarding the incident on X, writing they responded to the collapse of the driveway "and resulting gas leak" in the early hours of Tuesday morning, noting the Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department and the Los Angeles County Fire Department "responded and closed the private road, and identified the gas leak."

"The City’s Building Safety Division and Southern California Gas Company are working to assess the situation," they wrote. "At this time, the City red tagged five homes (prohibited entry). The City’s Building Safety Division and Southern California Gas Company will continue to assess the situation to determine safety concerns for the surrounding area, and will provide updates as they become available."

No evacuations have been ordered in the area. However, the city added that they are "actively monitoring and responding to" other issues associated with coastal erosion, specifically in areas along the "Pacific Coast Highway in the Palisades Fire burn area and at Westward Beach due to strong waves and high tides."

"The City is preparing for potential strong storms, strong waves, heavy rain, mudslides, and coastal erosion that are possible along the entire Southern California coast due to the forecast strong El Niño conditions," they added.

According to Realtor.com, Cage purchased the 4,000-square-foot home in 2024 for $10.5 million.

The modern home features a rooftop deck and a ground-level outdoor lounge area, with the inside featuring floor-to-ceiling windows, giving anyone who stepped inside the perfect ocean view.

It does not appear that Cage was home at the time of the driveway collapse, and no injuries have been reported.

Cage is known for his roles in "Fast Times at Ridgemont High," "Moonstruck," "Face/Off," "Gone In 60 Seconds" and "Leaving Las Vegas," which earned him an Academy Award.

Then I’m just going to sit and order two bottles of red wine and dissolve, and I don’t want to be that person, so I have to work."

item.title: Jennifer Lopez stuns in patterned swimsuit while soaking up final days of summer

Jennifer Lopez celebrated Labor Day with sunshine and a standout swimsuit look.

item.title: Former '60 Minutes' honcho says CBS News leaders wanted staff to 'compromise our principles'
item.description: Guy Campanile claimed he and his colleagues were fired from "60 Minutes" for refusing to compromise their journalism principles under new CBS leadership.
item.content:encoded:
Former CBS "60 Minutes" producer and managing editor Guy Campanile opened up about his firing earlier this year in a social media post on Tuesday, claiming he and his co-workers "refused to be accomplices in the destruction of the most prestigious news program on American television."

"We would not compromise our principles or reputations by jamming unverifiable notions or White House talking points into our reporting," Campanile wrote in a private Facebook post, according to reporters. "We objected when told to conduct interviews arranged by the administration. We insisted on asking the most challenging questions to business and political leaders without fear or favor." 

He added, "We did what reporters worth their salt do – we questioned authority...including our own bosses. That’s how the best newsrooms work. To be clear — we were told to leave because we insisted on doing our jobs."

SHARYN ALFONSI OUT AT ’60 MINUTES' AFTER FEUD WITH BARI WEISS, RIPS CBS FOR ‘CHILLING MESSAGE’ TO NEWSROOM

Campanile was one of several people fired from the network in May along with executive producer Tanya Simon, executive editor Draggan Mihailovich, senior producer Matthew Polevoy, and correspondents Sharyn Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega. The firings were part of the network's editor-in-chief, Bari Weiss' continued efforts to reorganize the long-running news program.

Though Campanile did not name anyone behind his firing, he called out "on-line opinionists" taking control of "institutions" like CBS News.

"Making matters worse is the cadre of self-described influencers and on-line opinionists who market themselves as 'journalists.' Some have been given control of our most precious reporting institutions — including CBS News. Many of these newsroom managers have never been exposed to the depths of poverty, the ravages of war or the heartbreak of disaster. Yet these dilettantes and their enablers make critical programming decisions based on what might trend on-line over the next few hours," he wrote.

NEW '60 MINUTES' PRODUCER HOPES TO CRACK DOWN ON 'RUMORS' LEAKED TO PRESS FOLLOWING DRAMATIC SHAKEUP

Ahead of the latest season premiere of "60 Minutes" on Sunday, Campanile wrote that he refuses to stay silent while media trust is "wrecked."

"As for my friends that remain at my former employer: Hold the line. Don’t give an inch because they will keep scraping away until there’s nothing left worth a da--," he closed.

A CBS News spokesperson declined to comment to Fox News Digital but pointed to past statements insisting accusations from former employees were not true.

CBS SHOOTS DOWN 'POLITICAL INTERFERENCE' CLAIMS IN AFTERMATH OF '60 MINUTES' FIRINGS

"60 Minutes" has produced several stories critical of the Trump administration, such as interviewing farmers who criticized Trump's tariffs and speaking with progressive American cardinals who opposed his immigration policies.

When asked for comment, Campanile told Fox News Digital his private Facebook post was intended to just be for friends and family and not for public consumption.

Longtime "60 Minutes" correspondent Scott Pelley was also fired shortly after Campanile following a bitter clash with Weiss and executive producer Nick Bilton over the direction of the series.

item.title: Ex-NFL star Shawne Merriman gives take on pro players trying to return to college: 'Pretty ridiculous'
item.description: Shawne Merriman called Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers eligibility controversy "ridiculous" and warns without guardrails, former pros returning won't stop.
item.content:encoded:
College football may be fully underway, but a dark cloud hovers over the landscape amid the controversy involving players who got professional experience trying to get back into the ranks with some of the best programs in the country, namely Lane Kiffin’s LSU Tigers program.

The latest from the SEC was an amended complaint filed on Tuesday morning in an Alabama federal court, which indicated the conference wishes to take some serious action against LSU after commissioner Greg Sankey stood in a Baton Rouge courtroom last week to argue the school, Lane Kiffin and the athletic department staffers were preventing the use of First Amendment rights to govern the conference.

All of this to say college athletics has reached a point where former NFL and Maryland Terrapins linebacker Shawne Merriman can’t believe his eyes.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"I think it’s pretty ridiculous," he told OutKick about athletes returning to college to get their fifth year of eligibility despite going pro just months ago. "Look, I’ve met Lane Kiffin plenty of times. I think he’s great. I got no problem for him wanting to win by putting whoever he can on the roster and making the situation better.

"But there have to be guardrails, because it won’t stop here if you don’t stop it now. That’s the issue."

Merriman added that college athletics has "always been pure," and even with name, image and likeness (NIL) deals becoming a key component of why these athletes are willing to stay, or even return, to Division I sports, he believes there was some decorum everyone could agree on.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Now, it’s a free-for-all, with athletes jumping through the transfer portal chasing the next biggest check from colleges and universities to play for them. And with the NCAA ruling that college athletes have five years to use five seasons of eligibility, players like tight end Dae’Quan Wright, who played four years of college football before going undrafted and getting cut by the Cleveland Browns, are trying to return to play their fifth year in college.

"There has to be some guardrails with the transferring," Merriman added. "Guys being able to take NIL money, then getting up to leave and go to another program. Now, it’s just kind of the tipping point where a former professional athlete can go back into college. It’s just too much. If they don’t stop it now, it’s never going to stop."

Amid the college debacle, the NFL sent a memo to its clubs reminding them that players who return to college to play wouldn’t be eligible to be signed during the season. Furthermore, those players are no longer eligible for an NFL Draft, meaning they would have to join an NFL team at some point in a future season as a free agent.

But if that player does end up in a locker room, how would the rest of the team react knowing what happened? Will there be some distain from teammates?

"I think it’s going to be a silent yes," Merriman responded when posed the same question. "I don’t think a lot of guys will be vocal to it. I even think the NFL is going to have a silence behind it but have a problem with it. There’s been plenty of guys through the past few decades or so that just didn’t cut it, right? For whatever reason, they didn’t make the roster. Maybe they got injured, maybe the coaching staff saw they didn’t line up with their scheme. Plenty of reasons, so why do you get an opportunity to go back and do something else and return?

"Look, I don’t think the return will be taken the right way trying to get back into an NFL locker room because, at that point, all kinds of things will be questioned -- Integrity, motive, what kind of guy this is. I’m not going to say that will be the pinpoint conversations, but I think there will be a lot of silence behind closed doors with people having a problem with it."

What plays out in the courtroom remains to be seen, but as a team like LSU continues its pursuit of a national championship, Merriman knows this controversy can pose a threat to focus.

COLTS GM CHRIS BALLARD RIPS NFL PLAYERS RETURNING TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL: 'STUPIDEST S--- I’VE EVER HEARD'

"It’s a distraction. There’s a high-risk, low reward to get a couple of guys go out and go play," he said. "What about the rest of the team that’s got to answer questions? Instead of talking about the game, they’re talking about this. So, I just think that the risk is just too high, and the reward is too low to fight this battle, especially now with the SEC and committee stepping in as a whole."

Merriman is also focused on the college landscape considering his son, Justin Merriman, is on a path to Division I football in his own right. Justin is one of the top quarterback prospects for the 2029 class, a 6-foot-3-and-a-half quarterback for St. Frances Academy (Baltimore, Maryland), the no. 2-ranked high school program in the country by MaxPreps.

The elder Merriman said he’s grateful to watch his son at this stage of his football career, where he can offer guidance and direction in a world completely different from when he was on his way to playing for Maryland before becoming a first-round NFL Draft pick by the San Diego Chargers.

"He makes all his own decisions, but to be that resource for him and let him know some of this guidance and which directions to take has been really cool for me," Merriman said.

Justin and St. Frances Academy will be taking on IMG Academy later this season, and it’s not just a clash between two of the top teams in the country, but the latest chapter of a bitter rivalry for these two programs. They kick off on Nov. 13 at St. Frances, which Merriman said is likely to be the most-watched high school football game in the country this season.

item.title: IndyCar champ Alex Palou on the importance of appreciating success after his fourth straight series title
item.description: Alex Palou tells OutKick he pinches himself daily over his four consecutive IndyCar titles with Chip Ganassi Racing and what drives the team's fire.
item.content:encoded:
For the fifth time in six years — and the fourth year straight — Chip Ganassi Racing's Alex Palou is the NTT IndyCar Series champion.

It's an incredible run, with only Sébastien Bourdais matching his four-straight title run, having done so in the mid-2000s before the Indy Racing League and the Champ Car World Series merger.

But while he's far from a stranger when it comes to winning championships, Palou told OutKick over Zoom on Monday that he's always taking time to appreciate his successes.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

"Every single day, man, like, almost every single day," Palou said. "I kind of need to pinch myself and be like, 'It's incredible to be in this position.' I never thought in my entire life that I would have an opportunity like this. I'm just trying to enjoy as much as I can because I know at some point it's going to end, right? And there's going to be someone else sitting in this seat, in this chair, and I just want to make sure I take it all in."

Palou's run has been incredible, especially in a series renowned for its competitive balance and the need to master three totally different styles of racetrack.

As much as that comes down to Palou, it also comes down to the environment at CGR and the people who have worked to get the No. 10 Honda to victory lane for so many years.

"It's very tough to stay up top... and the thing I like the most is the fire that everybody has at Chip Ganassi Racing," the 29-year-old from Spain said. "Although they have already won 18 championships, there's people that are in my car who have been for each one of those 18 championships, and they still work as much as they can to make sure that we can continue to battle and fight for the championship."

That team is about to see a big change as Palou's longtime teammate Scott Dixon will move to Arrow McLaren in 2027 after 25 years with CGR.

While the new driver of the No. 9 has yet to be announced at the time of writing, Palou will likely be the most experienced driver on the team, which also includes Kyffin Simpson in the No. 8.

Still, he doesn't expect to see his role on the team change in any way.

"I don't think it's going to change much, honestly. Like, I think the way we have of working at Chip Ganassi Racing," Palou said. "There's not a lead driver that kind of manages a bit more than everybody else or has more say."

He said that he expected it to work that way, especially in his first season on the team when he was driving alongside not just Dixon, but another bona fide motorsports legend: NASCAR great Jimmie Johnson.

"So I thought that I had like zero say on how we were going to operate and how we were going to prepare the cars and stuff, and that was not the case," he explained. "They treated me like another one like them. I had the same (input) as they did, and I think nowadays it works the same way with Kyffin... whoever is fastest at practice, that's the leader of the team that day."

INDYCAR'S FREEDOM 250 GRAND PRIX SPECTACLE IN WASHINGTON, DC DRAWS MASSIVE TV RATINGS

Looking to the future, Palou isn't just chasing more championships; he's also going to have a big part in the future of the series.

He was front and center at the series' marquee events, including the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, a massive success for the series.

"It was a big win for IndyCar, and also that showed what we're able to achieve," he said, before joking that maybe hitting the highs of last month's race around the Nation's capital were lofty. "I think that was a 12 out of 10 as an event in general."

But the series is in a good place and will only get better with the introduction of its first new chassis in well over a decade, the Dallara IR-28.

Palou tested the new car on the Indianapolis Motor Speedway in August, and is set to give it a shakedown on the track's iconic oval on Thursday.

The early returns are very good.

"I mean, it was incredible," he said. "I would love to race it next year instead of in '28, but honestly, I think everyone at IndyCar and both engine manufacturers, Honda (and Chevrolet), have done incredible work on developing this new car. We had like almost zero issues."

He then pointed out that this car has more than a year of development before it makes its in-race debut in 2028.

"I think, already now, if the car was on track with the other IndyCars, that car would win the race by far," he explained. "So, yeah, I'm excited to see what we're able to do and achieve with the car if we work for a full year."

Now that's a sentence that could make other IndyCar teams nervous: Alex Palou getting behind the wheel of an even faster car.

item.title: MAC files appeal to FBS committee to overturn Western Michigan-Michigan game, declare Broncos as winners
item.description: The MAC filed a formal NCAA appeal claiming the Western Michigan Broncos should be recognized as winners after a replay protocol error at Michigan.
item.content:encoded:
For a few minutes, the most stunning result of the early part of the college football season seemed to be the Western Michigan Broncos upsetting the heavily favored Michigan Wolverines at Michigan Stadium.

The Big House. Bryce Underwood, one of the most heavily promoted recruits of the past decade. New head coach Kyle Whittingham, known for his stability, consistency and avoiding major upsets while with the Utah Utes. And the Broncos took a 12-7 lead with just 38 seconds remaining and the Wolverines out of timeouts.

Everyone knows what happened next. Underwood's first Hail Mary attempt flew out of the back of the endzone, with the game clock on the broadcast and scoreboard showing 0:00. Game over. But after a poorly-explained review determined that there should have been an additional second added, Underwood was given a second opportunity. JJ Buchanan came down with it, and Wolverines fans stormed the field.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSIBLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Nearly everyone outside Michigan was perplexed, or downright angry, about the outcome. The Big Ten's explanation didn't make anything better either, with the conference saying the clocks were strobe-synced prior to the game, but that another clock viewed during the replay process had determined there was a second left. Even though the synced cameras showed zero seconds remaining.

Initially, it seemed like that would be the end of it. Western Michigan staff said they communicated with the Big Ten, reviewed the footage and were satisfied that proper procedure had been followed. Tuesday afternoon, though, that all changed.

The Mid-American Conference released a statement, announcing they'd filed a formal appeal to the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that those two bodies recognize the Broncos as the true winners of the game.

"After further study and investigation, it is now evident that replay protocol was not properly followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock at the conclusion of the Western Michigan vs. Michigan football game," the statement says. "The established replay protocol requires that the game clock displayed on the program feed be used in determining whether time remained. Instead, the Big Ten Conference replay crew relied upon the clock feed embedded within its replay system. As a result, one second was placed back on the game clock and an additional play was awarded."

CRAIG CARTON BLASTS MICHIGAN FANS FOR STORMING FIELD AFTER CONTROVERSIAL WIN: 'THEY’RE A BUNCH OF MORONS'

Interestingly, they also stress that the appeal isn't contesting the correct amount of time on the clock, just that the rules were improperly applied.

"This was not a judgment regarding the proper amount of time to place on the clock," it continues. "It was an error in the application of the established replay protocol governing this specific end-of-game timing situation. Had the protocol been properly followed and the program-feed clock been used, no additional play would have been awarded, and Western Michigan would have won the game, 12–7."

MICHIGAN FANS CALLED OUT ON SOCIAL MEDIA FOR RUSHING FIELD AFTER WOLVERINES STEAL WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN

The conference, as a result, want the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee and College Football to recognize the Western Michigan Broncos as the "actual winner."

"The MAC is requesting that those bodies recognize Western Michigan as the actual winner of the game for purposes of their respective rankings, evaluations and selection deliberations, and take such other corrective action as may be within their authority," the statement concludes.

So what does the NCAA rule book actually say about this procedure, and does the MAC have a point? The closest relevant rule seems to govern what video evidence can be evaluated as part of a review. And while it's not overwhelmingly clear what the proper procedure should be, there is an indication that the "televised production" should be used when evaluating video evidence.

"All reviews shall be based upon video evidence provided by and coming directly from the televised production of the game or from other video means available to the replay official that is also available to the television producer," the rule says.

So what chance does the MAC have at getting the result overturned? Very little. Even if there is some truth to this appeal, and the result was unfair to Western Michigan, it's a near impossibility that an FBS Committee overturns a result that was determined on the field. And it goes without saying that big programs like Michigan are a near-certainty to get the benefit of the doubt in these types of cases.

But the MAC at least showed some backbone and support for its member school after that debacle and what it cost them. Western Michigan may have contended for a College Football Playoff spot, with the benefit of a win over a top-20 opponent, had the game ended at 0:00.

In response, the Big Ten issued a statement of their own, saying, "The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter."

Sums up where both sides are, and why this controversy will never reach a satisfactory resolution for all involved parties.

item.title: American Bishop Robert Barron calls out St. Paul's Cathedral in UK over nightclub partnership
item.description: Roman Catholic Bishop Robert Barron blasted St. Paul's Cathedral for its multi-year Fabric nightclub concert deal, calling it a surrender to secularism.
item.content:encoded:
Bishop Robert Barron criticized London’s historic St. Paul’s Cathedral on Monday over its new partnership with a nightclub company, arguing the venue's upcoming concert series undermines its status as a sacred space.

The Christian Post reported that the Church of England is facing widespread backlash after St. Paul’s Cathedral in London signed a multiyear agreement to host concerts inside the building with Fabric, a nightclub company that lost its license approximately 10 years ago after two drug-related deaths. While the cathedral has worked with the nightclub company before, this latest agreement has sparked an international firestorm of controversy.

"Word has just come down that St. Paul’s Cathedral in London — the second most important church in the Anglican world — has imitated Canterbury Cathedral in permitting ‘raves,’ nightclub-like entertainments, to take place in its confines," he began.

TOURIST'S CHURCH CLOTHING HACK LEAVES TRAVELERS SHARPLY DIVIDED OVER SACRED-SITE ETIQUETTE

He blasted those who have already emerged to defend the move, saying "The usual reasons for acquiescing to this have been trotted out: reaching out to the young, trying to get with the times, etc. But this development simply shows that the leadership of the Church of England has lost any sense of the crucial distinction between the sacred and the secular."

Barron argued that the whole point of a sacred space is that it is specifically set apart from the mundane, secular world and is meant to "reorient us toward the divine."

"Accordingly, in the properly sacred space, one is lifted out of the conventional and introduced into the numinous. This is why Christian cathedrals are filled with images of the saints and angels and why their interiors are meant first to disorient us and then to reorient us toward the divine," he wrote.

"The contemporary West is, quite literally, the first culture in human history that is in danger of collapsing the sacred into the secular, or better, losing any sense of the difference between the two," he added further. "This is doing enormous damage, especially to young people, whose lives have been flattened into a preoccupation with money, worldly success, and material things. He concluded, "Having ‘raves’ in the nave of one of the most sacred spaces in the Christian world is, I’m sad to say, another sign of our pitiful surrender to ideological secularism."

According to the BBC, the events held at the event venue will be concerts rather than raves.

"Under the partnership, Fabric will be the cathedral's exclusive partner for such events until 2030. The first concert is due to take place on 29 October, although the artist has not been announced," the BBC reported. "Fabric co-founder Cameron Leslie called the deal ‘an extraordinary and unexpected coming together of two very different parts of London.’"

The BBC quoted Sandra Lynes Timbrell, the cathedral's director of visitor engagement, who expressed hope that a "carefully curated programme of exceptional concerts" would draw people who otherwise had not visited the cathedral.

The controversy mirrors a 2024 dispute at Canterbury Cathedral, which hosted sold-out 90s "silent discos" that critics mocked as a "rave in the nave."

More recently, Canterbury cathedral featured the "Hear Us" art installation, using large stickers simulating graffiti, reportedly inspired by working with "marginalised communities and a team of skilled artists to create vibrant handwritten literature responding to the question: ‘What would you ask God?’" The project was conceived by poet Alex Vellis and curator Jacquiline Creswell.

Fox News Digital reached out to Bishop Robert Barron and Saint Paul's Cathedral and did not receive an immediate reply.

While cathedral leaders argue secular events help attract younger generations, some young believers say church leaders are misjudging what youth actually want.

Catholic actor David Henrie recently told Fox News Digital that he sees young people turning away from secular trends and seeking out traditional faith. Henrie noted an uptick in youth attending traditional Latin Mass services in the United States specifically because they are searching for a clear contrast to modern culture.

"I've seen it coming. I was one of those people who was not living a Christian life and then suddenly found the world was completely empty and was searching for something other worldly," Henrie said. "That's why I think you're seeing kids flock to the faith right now. It's because they're tired of the world."

"[T]hey want 'Lord of the Rings Catholicism,'" Henrie said. "You know, they want bells, smells, ancient expressions of the liturgy. That's where the young people are flocking right now. That's why you're seeing the Latin Mass booming."

Catholic leaders across the U.S. have reported sharp increases in the number of adult converts. A recent Gallup poll also found that 42% of young men now say religion is "very important" in their lives, a 14-percentage-point jump from the previous year.

item.description: Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport revealed their reasons for disliking LeBron James during the premiere of OutKick's "The Craig Carton Show."
item.content:encoded:
Craig Carton and Michael Rapaport have more in common than being die-hard New York Knicks fans: They also share a strong dislike for LeBron James.

Rapaport joined Carton for the premiere of OutKick’s "The Craig Carton Show" releasing on Tuesday, where he called the Philadelphia 76ers star a player he loves to hate. Carton admitted that while he respects James’ game, his No. 1 reason for his dislike stems from an off-the-court incident in 2017.

"I'll tell you the number one reason I'm not a LeBron guy. Number one. There's—it's and it's a clear-cut number one for me, and I think I'm the only guy that views it this way, and it p----es me off, all right. Years ago, when he was in Cleveland, and our country is going through racial issues," Carton said on the premiere of his new show.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"In my opinion, he invented a story that the people spray-painted racial epithets on the gate leading up his driveway."

The Associated Press reported at the time, citing police, that unidentified vandals spray-painted the N-Word on the front gate of James' $20 million home in Brentwood. Police said the incident was reported at around 6:45 a.m. local time and nearly three hours later property management covered it up. No arrests were ever made. 

Carton said that he believed James used the event as a vehicle to include himself in the larger conversation at the time.

"And to me, I'm like, look, there's real racial issues in our country. We acknowledge them. For a guy who's such a prominent African-American to try to get in on the conversation by inventing something that never took place. Dead to me," Carton said. "No one talks about it. It's been forgotten because it never happened. No one has the balls to ask—ask him about it, and I'm like, how do we forget the fact that he intruded himself into this serious conversation about race?"

While Rapaport shares Carton’s disdain for the NBA legend, his reason is much more personal. The actor said he had been cool with James and that they had first met during his rookie year with the Cleveland Cavaliers.

A few years later, Rapaport was with his kids, who were 5 and 7 at the time, and James spurned the kids' request for a picture.

"I don't know what he got up bug up his a-- about Michael Rapaport. I had never said anything bad about him. Never said anything," Rapaport said. "I brought my little kids. They were like five and seven, right? And he like Heismaned."

After that point, Rapaport was turned off by James. Prior to the incident with his kids, Rapaport said he had never said anything bad about the then-Cavaliers star.

"I never said anything bad about him. And I think it was a rumor that a friend of mine might have a girl with a friend, and I was like, that has nothing to do with—these are little kids. And that was when I was like, ‘You’re done,’" Rapaport said.

Fox News Digital reached out to the White House, Apple, Google and Paramount for comment.

item.title: SCOTUS rejects Missouri GOP bid to use revised congressional map in midterms
item.description: SCOTUS rejects Missouri Republicans' emergency bid over congressional maps, with Justice Kavanaugh ruling without comment and leaving the GOP-backed map blocked for the midterms.
item.content:encoded:
Justice Brett Kavanaugh on Tuesday denied Missouri's emergency appeal without comment, leaving in place the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling blocking the state's revised Republican-backed congressional map from being used in November's general election. 

Kavanaugh acted alone and did not refer the application to the full Supreme Court.

The decision means Missouri will conduct the general election using its 2022 congressional districts after the state high court ruled the newer map never legally took effect because a voter-backed referendum suspended the law before it could go into effect.

Missouri Attorney General Catherine Hanaway had asked the Supreme Court to intervene after the Missouri Supreme Court ruled last week that the state's revised congressional map could not be used in November, despite having been used during last month's primary election. The emergency appeal was directed to Kavanaugh because he oversees emergency applications arising from the Eighth Circuit.

MISSOURI AG FILES PETITION ASKING SUPREME COURT TO REVIVE TRUMP-BACKED REDISTRICTING MAP

The revised map, backed by President Donald Trump and Missouri Republicans, was designed to make Democratic Rep. Emanuel Cleaver's Kansas City-area district more favorable to Republicans, with the goal of expanding the GOP's congressional delegation from 6-2 to 7-1.

The Missouri Supreme Court ruled the referendum petition filed by opponents after lawmakers approved the new districts prevented the map from taking effect unless voters ultimately approve it. The court concluded the congressional map adopted after the 2020 census "remains in full force and effect for the November 2026 general election."

Hanaway argued the state faced an unprecedented situation after administering its primary election under one set of congressional districts only to be ordered to use another for the general election.

In its emergency filing, Missouri told the Supreme Court it now faced "the unprecedented scenario of being forced to apply a starkly different congressional map in the 2026 General Election." The state argued election officials were uncertain whether they could comply with the Missouri Supreme Court's order with voting scheduled to begin within days.

MISSOURI HIGH COURT BLOCKS GOP-BACKED CONGRESSIONAL MAPS AHEAD OF MIDTERMS; TRUMP BLASTS 'RIDICULOUS' RULING

"Only this Court can prevent Missouri from being forced to disenfranchise hundreds of thousands of voters; and only this Court can ensure that Missouri hosts a timely and lawful federal congressional election," the application said.

Hanaway also called the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling "catastrophic."

"We have just appealed yesterday's catastrophic ruling to the Supreme Court of the United States," she said after filing the emergency appeal. "We look forward to the Court's prompt review of this critical matter, as our ability to hold timely and lawful congressional elections hangs in the balance."

Opponents urged the justices to reject the request, arguing there was no genuine emergency because Missouri officials created the timing problem themselves.

GEORGIA REDISTRICTING BATTLE REVIVED AFTER APPEALS COURT OVERTURNS FEDERAL COURT DECISION

In their response, they argued the state's Secretary of State waited until "the last possible day" to challenge the referendum after implementing the revised map during the congressional primary, hoping the courts would refuse to order a return to the previous districts so close to the general election.

"The Emergency Application for Stay does not present a real emergency," they wrote.

They also argued the Supreme Court should not "reward the Secretary's scheme to outsmart Missouri voters, Missouri law, and the Missouri Supreme Court" by allowing the state to use a map the state's highest court concluded "is not the law and has never been the law."

Kavanaugh's denial leaves the Missouri Supreme Court's ruling in place, meaning Missouri's 2022 congressional map will remain in effect for the November general election.

item.title: Aaron Donald will not travel to Australia for Rams opener against 49ers as team ramp-up process not complete
item.description: Aaron Donald won't travel to Melbourne for the Rams' opener against the San Francisco 49ers, with his season debut now targeting Monday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Rams are running a marathon rather than a sprint with Aaron Donald. That’s why Donald wasn’t included in the team's travel party for Thursday night’s matchup against the San Francisco 49ers in Australia.

Because Donald is not going to play in the opener, Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters on Tuesday.

This is a mild surprise given that McVay said in recent days that all the team's players would travel to Australia.

"He's doing a great job," McVay said of Donald. "I think he'll be ready to go sooner rather than later, but we're making a decision that we think is best for him and for our team.

"He's as great a competitor as there is, wants to be out there, wants to influence and effect positive change for us. But I think he also understands there's a necessary ramp up."

Ultimately, Donald and the Rams decided it was better for the 35-year-old defensive lineman, who came out of retirement on Aug. 30, to continue to prepare for the long haul of the looming season rather than plug him in immediately.

Donald has not played in a game since January 2024.

'WE BACK': AARON DONALD RETURNS TO THE RAMS AND A DEFENSE NOW LOADED WITH MYLES GARRETT AND OTHERS

Donald's next opportunity to play will be on Sept. 21 when the Rams host the New York Giants on Monday Night Football.

That gives Donald an extra 10 days to acclimate and prepare for his season.

And why is that important to the Rams?

They see themselves as not just part of the Super Bowl conversation but at the center of it. They felt that way before Donald rejoined the team and still do heading into Thursday night’s game against the 49ers without him.

That's the reason McVay spent a minute discussing the depth of his defensive line.

The Rams want to simply make sure Donald has every chance to prepare for the long haul of the season by getting more time to prepare for its demands.

The last thing the team wants, a source said, is to put Donald in the lineup just a couple of weeks after returning to team practices and expose him to a soft-tissue injury that could linger throughout the season.

So, again, everyone is looking at this as a marathon to run over 16 games and the postseason rather than sprinting off the line in Week 1.

COACH SEAN MCVAY ON AARON DONALD RETURN TO THE LOS ANGELES RAMS: 'WE ARE NOT AT THAT POINT QUITE YET'

The Rams are scheduled to depart Los Angeles International Airport on Tuesday night, Sept. 8, for the approximately 15-to-16-hour flight to Melbourne.

The team will touch down on Thursday morning (in Australia) due to the 14-hour time difference. The club will basically lose all of Wednesday en route.

They will check in to their hotel Thursday morning and play the game at 10:35 a.m. on Friday in Melbourne.

The game is scheduled to kick off at 8:35 p.m. ET on Thursday in the United States.

item.title: Judge orders Alex Murdaugh murder retrial moved to nearby county
item.description: Alex Murdaugh's double murder retrial moves to Sumter County after a judge ruled Colleton County's jury pool was too compromised for a fair trial.
item.content:encoded:
A South Carolina judge on Tuesday granted a request by Alex Murdaugh that the double-murder retrial for the disgraced attorney be relocated to a new venue.

Judge Debra McCaslin ruled that the trial will take place in Sumter County. Defense lawyers argued that Colleton County's jury pool was tainted by the highly covered original trial.

In her order, McCaslin wrote that Murdaugh can receive a fair trial in Sumter County, adding that it offers adequate security measures, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities to conduct proceedings.

ALEX MURDAUGH'S 'CHARLESTON OR BUST' PRAYER SHOT DOWN BY PROSECUTORS IN FIGHT OVER 'HOLY CITY' RETRIAL

"The judge considered several factors including the financial impact on Colleton County, the convenience of witnesses, courthouse security, transportation and security of Murdaugh, courtroom facilities, and technological capabilities," the order states.

Murdaugh's attorneys had suggested Charleston or Richland County courthouses for the venue transfer before McCaslin made her ruling.

ALEX MURDAUGH RETURNS TO COURT AS DEFENSE ARGUES FOR RETRIAL MOVE AFTER CLERK SCANDAL POISONED JURY POOL

Fox News Digital has reached out to Murdaugh's attorneys and prosecutors.

Murdaugh was granted a new trial after the South Carolina Supreme Court determined his right to a fair proceeding was violated when it found that former Colleton County Clerk of Court Becky Hill improperly influenced jurors during his 2023 murder trial.

ALEX MURDAUGH WINS NEW TRIAL AFTER COURT CLERK ALLEGEDLY TOLD JURORS NOT TO BE 'FOOLED' BY DEFENSE

As a result, the court unanimously overturned his 2023 convictions and two life sentences.

Murdaugh is charged with murder and weapons offenses for the June 2021 shooting deaths of his wife, Maggie, and 22-year-old son, Paul, at their family estate.

At his 2023 trial, Murdaugh admitted to misleading investigators about his location shortly before his wife and son were shot, but he has consistently denied killing either of them.
